samples.summary: `checkSlidesTargeting` dereferences an unchecked reader result — `before.value.x` throws a TypeError and aborts the whole oracle run
samples.evidence: Line 534-535: `const before = await readReader(page, "slides.elementCenter", [target.id]); await page.mouse.click(before.value.x, before.value.y);`. `readReader` returns `{ok:false, error}` (no `value`) on refusal — the very loop just above (lines 512-516) explicitly tolerates that case for the same reader (`if (!point.ok) { problems.push(...); continue; }`). If `slides.elementCenter(elements[0].id)` refuses (element nudged/moved off-slide by a previous check, canvas not measurable, current slide mismatch), `before.value` is `undefined` and `before.value.x` throws. The throw propagates out of `checkSlidesTargeting`, past the `try` at line 1402 into the outer `catch` (line 1467) which re-throws for any message not mentioning Chromium — so instead of one reported failure the script dies with an opaque TypeError and every later check (sheet toolbar, control inventory, run colour, undo capability, seeded fault, prediction funnel) never runs. Same shape for `after`/`selection` reads, which are guarded, and for `restUndo.value` at line 530 (that one only mis-reports rather than crashing).

samples.summary: `slides.elements`' `text` cannot observe in-flight typing — the slides store is written only on text-edit COMMIT, so the documented "typing is observable" contract and the brief built on it are wrong
samples.evidence: `textOfElement` (bridge.ts:218-226) reads `element.data.blocks` out of `store.read()`, and the bridge doc at line 69 claims "typing into a text box is observable without a second reader". But the slides editor's in-place text box keeps the edit local until commit: editor.ts:3984-3988 states "The editor's source of truth (Yorkie) is only ever touched on commit", and the store write happens in the `onCommit` path (exitEditMode('commit'), editor.ts:2305-2307/3545). While edit mode is active, `slides.elements` still reports the OLD text and `MemSlidesStore.canUndo()` (memory.ts:1819) is still false because no `batch()` has run. scripts/agent/charters-ui/slide-author.md and the `content-and-undo` brief (personas.json:66) instruct the explorer to "make one edit and confirm it turned true" and to type then undo — if the chosen edit is typing, `slides.canUndo` reads false and `slides.elements` reads unchanged, producing exactly the manufactured 'the app swallowed my edit / undo is not tracked' finding this harness exists to prevent. There is also no reader exposing text-edit mode, so the explorer cannot distinguish the two states.

samples.summary: The slides harness never wires `store.onChange` to `editor.markDirty()/render()`, so store-only mutations (toolbar Undo/Redo, Arrange, alignment) leave the canvas and overlay stale
samples.evidence: The real host does this explicitly: slides-view.tsx:1051-1059 `const offChange = store.onChange(() => { editor.markDirty(); editor.render(); ... })`, with the comment that the editor "doesn't know the underlying data shifted under it". `SlidesEditorImpl` has no store subscription of its own (no `store.onChange` in editor.ts), and none of the toolbar controls repaint (`grep markDirty|requestRender packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar` matches only apply-font-family.ts) — e.g. `UndoRedoGroup` (global-controls.tsx:55) only calls `store?.undo()`. In the hunt harness the canvas therefore keeps painting the pre-mutation frame until some unrelated interaction requests a render. Readers read the store so predictions still resolve, but the mounted surface diverges from the product it is meant to stand in for, and selection chrome for elements removed by an undo stays painted.

samples.summary: `data-hunt-harness-ready` does not gate on the lazily-imported slides toolbar, so the page can be declared ready with zero toolbar controls
samples.evidence: The comment at lines 563-568 asserts "by the time anything reads this page the toolbar's chunk has arrived", but nothing enforces that: `SlidesToolbarLazy` starts loading when React first renders the Suspense subtree, while `setStatus("ready")`/`controller.setReady(true)` (lines 484-485) fire when the *effect's* `await import("@wafflebase/slides")` + `initializeEditor` finish. The two are independent promises; if the toolbar's chunk (or its own dependency graph, resolved request-by-request on a cold Vite dev server) lands after the engine's, `dom.controls` reads an empty toolbar at a moment the driver considers the surface ready — precisely the failure the persona brief warns about ("a run that reads it once at rest will think the surface has no controls"). The runner's `waitUntil: "networkidle"` (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:228) makes this unlikely but does not make it impossible, and nothing asserts the slides toolbar renders.

samples.summary: `slides.currentSlideIndex` answers `null` for a state every other slides reader refuses on, hiding a broken harness behind a plausible-looking value
samples.evidence: Lines 459-464 return `at < 0 ? null : at + 1` when the editor's current slide id is not in the store, whereas `currentSlide()` (lines 229-236) refuses with "the editor reports slide … but the store has no such slide — the harness is broken, not the product" for exactly that condition. A caller reading `null` cannot tell "no slide is current" from "the harness is inconsistent", and a prediction comparing `currentSlideIndex` across a slide operation would silently record a held/violated verdict against a broken state instead of an unevaluable refusal.

samples.summary: The slides reader block was inserted between `sheet.cellCenter`'s doc comment and its implementation, so that comment now documents `slides.elements`
samples.evidence: Lines 408-414 ("Viewport coordinates of a cell's centre … Mirrors `getCellCenterClientPoint` in the interaction harness.") are immediately followed by `// --- slides ---` at line 415 and the `slides.elements` docblock; the `"sheet.cellCenter"` implementation it describes is now at line 526, 118 lines away and carrying no summary of its own. Anyone reading top-down attributes the cell-centre contract to the slides reader.

finding.evidence: Line 534-535: `const before = await readReader(page, "slides.elementCenter", [target.id]); await page.mouse.click(before.value.x, before.value.y);`. `readReader` returns `{ok:false, error}` (no `value`) on refusal — the very loop just above (lines 512-516) explicitly tolerates that case for the same reader (`if (!point.ok) { problems.push(...); continue; }`). verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described and is not guarded. `readReader` (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:292-296) resolves to `{ok:false, error}` with no `value` on rejection, and lines 534-535 dereference `before.value.x`/`before.value.y` with no `before.ok` check. Refusal is a real, modelled outcome for `slides.elementCenter`: bridge.ts:487-523 throws via `refuse()` for a missing id, a missing canvas, a non-finite point, and an off-slide centre — and the loop at verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:500-504 explicitly handles `!point.ok` for the same reader, then `continue`s (no early return), so control still reaches line 534 with the same element. On refusal the resulting TypeError escapes `checkSlidesTargeting` (called at line 1419 inside the try at 1402), and the outer catch at 1467-1474 re-throws anything not mentioning Chromium install text, so the script dies and checkSheetToolbar (1424), checkControlInventory (1429), checkRunColor (1434), checkUndoCapability (1439), checkSeededFault (1444) and checkPredictionFunnel (1456) never run. The secondary claim about `restUndo.value` (530) reading `.value` without `.ok` also holds (mis-report, not crash). Missing-guard crash that aborts a CI gate precisely when a regression is present — correctness lane, blocking.

finding.summary: `slides.elements`' `text` cannot observe in-flight typing — the slides store is written only on text-edit COMMIT, so the documented "typing is observable" contract and the brief built on it are wrong
finding.evidence: `textOfElement` (bridge.ts:218-226) reads `element.data.blocks` out of `store.read()`, and the bridge doc at line 69 claims "typing into a text box is observable without a second reader". But the slides editor's in-place text box keeps the edit local until commit: editor.ts:3984-3988 states "The editor's source of truth (Yorkie) is only ever touched on commit", and the store write happens in the `onCommit` path (exitEditMode('commit'), editor.ts:2305-2307/3545). verdict.reason: Every factual claim in the finding checks out in the repository. bridge.ts:68-69 does document that "typing into a text box is observable without a second reader", and textOfElement (bridge.ts:218-226) sources its text from currentSlide() -> handle.store.read() (bridge.ts:229-236, consumed by slides.elements at bridge.ts:424-439). The slides editor writes text to the store ONLY in the onCommit branch (editor.ts:4059-4082, inside store.batch), reached via exitEditMode('commit') -> tb.commit() (editor.ts:4270-4283) from click-outside (editor.ts:3532-3547), Escape/blur or slide change (editor.ts:1548, 2306, 2333); the editor's own comment at editor.ts:3983-3989 says the source of truth "is only ever touched on commit", and the live path only re-renders (editor.ts:4048-4058). MemSlidesStore.canUndo is undoStack-based (memory.ts:1819) and the stack only grows on a batch commit, so slides.canUndo stays false during in-flight typing. Edit mode is reachable with the explorer's vocabulary (goto|click|type|key|scroll|read|wait, hunt-ui-probe.mjs:44) because enterEditMode is wired to the keyboard handler (editor.ts:1512-1516; F2/Enter/printable entry noted at editor.ts:4029). I found no guard: the reader registry (bridge.ts:246-580) exposes no text-edit-mode reader, hunt-ui-expect.mjs has no slides/edit-mode handling, and the persona brief (personas.json:66) plus charter (slide-author.md:152-153) explicitly instruct "type into a text box, undo" and "make one edit and confirm canUndo turned true" without any mention that the edit must be committed first. So the documented contract is overstated in exactly the way described, and a grounded-but-false "edit was swallowed / undo not tracked" prediction is producible. No refutation ground applies (code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and it is a real behavioral/invariant gap in the sensor rather than style, security or design).
